The UAT sign-off covered core replenishment only, for the 25 store pilot cohort, covering ambient and dry goods categories. It explicitly did not extend to fresh categories, which remained in scope for a later phase, and it did not constitute acceptance of the overall programme. [1]

The sign-off wording was drafted by Ana Duarte on 21 January 2025 and signed by Lena Fischer on 22 January 2025. [1] [2]

In the UAT readiness review on 21 January 2025, Lena Fischer confirmed she was signing that ambient core replenishment works for twenty-five stores, not that the project is finished. [3] [4] [5] [6]

At the time of the sign-off wording, two UAT defects remained open, both the same root cause on case pack and minimum order quantity rounding. Both were scheduled for fix that week and neither was a blocker. [1]

Kwame Boateng later reported both rounding defects fixed and re-tested, with nine of nine scenarios now passing. [7]

Lena Fischer's email says "Signed and attached", but the signed attachment itself is not present in the supplied records; the email documents the confirmation of signature. [2]
